questions.q: What best distinguishes seasonality from a cycle?
options: Seasonality repeats at a fixed, known period; cycles rise and fall without a fixed length
Seasonality is random; cycles are predictable
Cycles always last exactly one year
questions.explain: A December peak comes back every 12 months, while business cycles vary in length, which makes them harder to separate from trend.

questions.q: In a multiplicative series, how does the seasonal swing behave?
options: It stays exactly the same size
It grows or shrinks in proportion to the level of the series
questions.explain: In value = trend x seasonal x noise, the seasonal factor scales with the trend, so peaks get taller as the series rises.

questions.q: Why did the classical decomposition in the lesson return 12 missing trend values for the 60-month series?
options: The centered moving average cannot be computed within six months of either end
Twelve values were dropped as outliers
A bug in the random number generator
questions.explain: With period=12, the centered moving average needs half a period on each side, so six values at each end are missing. STL avoids this.

questions.q: For daily data with a repeating weekly pattern, which period would you pass to seasonal_decompose?
questions.explain: The period is the number of observations in one repeat of the pattern: 7 days in a week, 12 months in a year.

questions.q: What is decomposition mainly used for?
options: Removing the need to split data into train and test
Understanding the structure of a series, such as trend, seasonality and noise, before choosing a model
Guaranteeing that the residual is zero
questions.explain: It is a diagnostic. It tells you what a model must handle, such as trend or seasonal terms or a log transform.
